Closes #279

## Summary

Bind each transfer to the quote the sender reviewed, and refuse confirmation when the quote, wallet connection, connectivity, or available balance cannot support it. This includes the original quote-freshness work and the subsequent locale, balance, and pending-connection corrections.

## Changes

- quoteBinding validates currency pairs, fingerprints priced inputs, checks signability, and reconciles canonical amounts. buildQuote adds a deterministic quote ID, fx.table source, and input fingerprint.
- QuoteCard displays quote source, ID, timestamps, expiry, and currency precision, with an explicit refresh action.
- SendMoney invalidates confirmation on priced-input and network changes, blocks expired quotes, and saves the reviewed quoteId in the transfer payload.
- French keyboard review parses localized input before canonical comparison. Portuguese repeated blur preserves the decimal separator. Canonical balance values are compared without parsing them through the input locale again.
- Confirmation requires the actual account returned by connect() and checks the bound amount against that account's balance. Rejected/incomplete connections and newly connected insufficient balances stop before transfer creation; affordable and exact-balance transfers remain supported.
- A confirmation version changes when its quote is invalidated or refreshed. After awaiting wallet connection, a superseded confirmation stops before transfer creation, including when connectivity drops and recovers during the wait. A live connectivity check also blocks current offline submission. The submission lock and finally release remain.
- Correct null-price feedback for an otherwise valid amount, update the four maintained test files to exercise the actual confirmation/result flow and canonical decimal contract, and apply the existing formatter to its fifteen flagged files. Exact money, offline blocking, submission lock, retry, receipt reconciliation, and no-create assertions remain.

## Compatibility and tradeoffs

Quote id/source and Transfer quoteId are additive; legacy records still parse. Identical priced inputs and clock produce the same quote ID; a later refresh produces a new one. Before dispatch, a network interruption clears the pending quote and requires a new review. Already-dispatched transfers retain their existing result handling.

## Current validation

Tested source: [17dd96c4](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/17dd96c4593fcd599286d263ed7cb72f6a4b7c20). The evidence-only child [91347ff3](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/91347ff3cb86c18f6d61cd299ad193a64785f47e) and subsequent report update [5b36c889](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/5b36c889de2c35af83bc0774ef813b03017a8e66) preserve all tested source files.

- Complete package selection: **485 passed, zero failed or skipped, across 49 files**, 54.94 seconds. This single combined execution includes the earlier quote, locale, balance, and connection cases, with no retries, exclusions, or snapshot changes.
- Existing Prettier check: passed, with configuration and ignores unchanged.
- npm audit --audit-level=critical: exit 0; zero critical findings. Remaining findings: 20 high, 12 moderate, and 2 low.
- Production build: passed; Vite reported 1.46 seconds.
- All 348 tracked blobs and modes matched the published source before execution and were unchanged afterward.
- Raw results, source manifest, exact command/configuration, and audit/build/formatter output: [report and evidence archive](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/5b36c889de2c35af83bc0774ef813b03017a8e66/work/validation/rf296-existing-suite-relay17-20261004/README.md).

## Validation boundary

Execution uses the repository's demonstration wallet and transfer service in jsdom. No live wallet/provider/settlement integration or application-performance improvement is established by these results. Dependency files are unchanged; the audit findings above remain. Raw output retains existing React/Vite warnings.

Earlier Chromium and local Lighthouse evidence remains tied to its original tested source and was not rerun in this continuation. The existing Vite development CSP/React-preamble issue is separate.

At the tested source, hosted [CI](https://github.com/RemitFlow/RemitFlow-Frontend/actions/runs/37194208479) and [Lighthouse CI](https://github.com/RemitFlow/RemitFlow-Frontend/actions/runs/37194208458) report action_required. Local formatting, tests, critical-audit, and build checks pass; hosted acceptance remains separate.

arguments.body:
Closes #531

## Changes

The backend Deployment now uses HTTP GET probes on port 3001:

- Startup: `/health`, 30-second timeout, 10 retries.
- Liveness: `/health/live`, 10-second interval.
- Readiness: `/health`, 5-second interval.

The existing `/health/live` route is registered before body parsing and dependency middleware, while preserving request IDs, headers, and request logging. It can respond while Redis-backed API rate limiting is stalled. `/health` remains the dependency-readiness route. The probe and endpoint behavior is documented in `k8s/README.md`.

The continuation repairs two inherited CI blockers: both workflow files used the unsupported workflow-root `retention-days` setting, and the secrets workflow called a deleted script. The invalid setting and its retention comments are removed, and the executable secrets checker is restored. The original build steps, secrets-check commands, and environment values are preserved.

The final two-file continuation reuses the completed secrets parser from PR #632, preserving the four existing allowed placeholder values. The checker rejects previously ignored hyphenated entries and additional Secret documents. Its existing workflow also runs when the checker or workflow itself changes; its jobs and commands remain unchanged.

## Validation

The application change at `165016556158601164594e7c10bb17196594784e` recorded the actual Express/IORedis flow: original liveness timed out at 5,208 ms; the repaired route returned HTTP 200 in 12 ms and 4 ms while an ordinary API request remained held by the limiter. These observations belong to that revision and were not rerun for the workflow and checker changes. No Kubernetes deployment was performed.

The workflow repair at `6927078b74878b4992ccf6e9ac66816ee24bc6e2` removed unsupported root settings while preserving the parsed jobs, triggers, environment values, and commands. The restored executable checker passed Bash syntax and accepted the committed placeholder manifest while rejecting a non-placeholder value and malformed `stringData`.

The final continuation at `c7ccbdfc800a69e9c8fa366942c715d57baab2ab` reuses checker blob `edc76dac363baab786dc4e1b19e557161a1b48b3` and workflow blob `b746db2adbaa501acf6429e8b801028b8a3eaf24`. Six exact-source before/after executions cover allowed placeholders, hyphenated and ordinary non-placeholder values, a preceding Secret document, an empty mapping, and a missing file. Allowed placeholders retain exit 0; non-placeholder values and malformed or incomplete inputs return nonzero. Bash syntax passed, and synthetic values were absent from stdout and stderr. Parsed workflow comparison preserves every job and command while adding the checker/workflow paths to the existing triggers.

The final published source and executable mode were read back. Current head: `c7ccbdfc800a69e9c8fa366942c715d57baab2ab`.

## Hosted execution

At the earlier workflow-repair revision, the [build run](https://github.com/Protocol-Guild/PayD/actions/runs/37184185218) and [secrets run](https://github.com/Protocol-Guild/PayD/actions/runs/37184185158) were `action_required`. The final parser continuation did not rerun the application build or establish hosted CI success. Maintainer acceptance remains separate from the execution results above.

arguments.body:
Closes #65

## Summary

Enforce position ownership at the service boundary and bind HTTP callers to server-provisioned identities. Forged wallet or role headers cannot disclose or mutate another user's positions. The authenticated routes also return valid v1 transaction receipts: authorized deposits return 201, and withdrawals and transaction history return 200.

This description covers the original position policy, the credential implementation, and the composed receipt correction at current head [`30457194`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/3045719435ee12f89018151d735c14b9de2000b8).

## Position access

- Every `/api/positions` route and `GET /api/vaults/:id/positions` requires an opaque Bearer token. `POSITION_CREDENTIALS` maps its SHA-256 digest to an exact subject and role; `X-Wallet-Address` and `X-Audit-Role` carry no position-access authority.
- Controllers pass the authenticated actor and operator binding into the shared `src/auth/positionAccess.js` service policy. Ordinary users see their own positions; missing and foreign IDs return the same 404 (`Position not found`), and cross-user list or summary filters return empty results. Malformed IDs also fail closed. A caller-selected body user cannot authorize a mutation.
- The existing `admin` and `auditor` policy remains: configured operators can inspect other positions and act for an explicit target user. Trusted in-process service callers retain their explicit-user interface; unscoped dumps remain forbidden.
- Missing, malformed, unknown or unconfigured credentials receive 401 and a Bearer challenge before position handling. Protected responses include `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

## Credential configuration and rollout

The dependency-free verifier accepts at most 100 immutable `{subject, role, tokenSha256}` entries. Subjects are bounded, trimmed identifiers without C0/C1 controls; roles are lowercase identifiers and digests must be unique. Malformed configuration stops startup without echoing its contents, and an empty registry denies position access. Verification compares every configured digest; the compiled registry does not retain raw tokens.

[README configuration and migration instructions](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/blob/3045719435ee12f89018151d735c14b9de2000b8/README.md#position-credentials) cover token generation, replacing header-only clients, and restart-based rotation and revocation. Credentials have no automatic expiry. This authenticates provisioned identities for the in-memory mock service; it does not prove control of a Stellar wallet. Public vault metadata and unrelated routes retain their existing access rules. No data migration is needed for the in-memory store.

## Valid v1 transaction receipts

The integration preserves both the authentication history at [`fcb73610`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/fcb73610d3252b61280a279df7c49b617d17e703) and the existing serializer repair at [`e45ca72d`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/e45ca72d87e0d0749e4a1e4d4ff87242cb8e6cbb). The serializer maps the mock provider's exact `SUCCESS` value to the v1 `confirmed` state and omits provider-only `network` and `ledger` fields from HTTP responses. Stored provider receipts and lifecycle records keep their original values.

Other fields still pass through the strict response validator, including unknown-field, unsupported-state, amount-precision and required-field checks. Position-controller composition preserves the authenticated `accessFrom(req)` bindings. Full withdrawal returns a null position. The previous post-write HTTP 500 caused by the receipt/response-contract mismatch is resolved.

## Current validation

Tested integration: [`e5ac9060f1fd771f1a91b89ad6c55823b9dcfef7`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/e5ac9060f1fd771f1a91b89ad6c55823b9dcfef7). Current head `30457194` adds the source-bound report without changing that product source.

One completed [native job](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Backend/actions/runs/37193117137/job/111409297443) ran on Ubuntu 24.04.5 with Node 22.23.3. Its workflow is hosted in the RemitFlow-Backend fork and explicitly checks out this YieldVault repository at `e5ac9060`.

- The same 17 contract cases reproduce **13 passes / 4 failures** on parent production `fcb73610` and **17 passes** on the integration.
- `npm test -- --test-concurrency=1`: **150 passed, zero failed or skipped**. This includes the unchanged 21-case ownership/HTTP suite and eight credential-helper cases, covering spoofed-header and unauthorized-mutation denials.
- `npm run validate:contracts`: all **eight unchanged response fixtures** validated.

| Actual application request | Parent | Integration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Authorized deposit | 500 | 201 |
| Authorized partial withdrawal | 500 | 200 |
| Authorized full withdrawal | 500 | 200 |
| First transaction-history page | 500 | 200 |
| Next transaction-history page | Not reached after first-page failure | 200 |

These requests use the actual Express application, Bearer middleware and in-memory mock provider. The reused fixture provisions a fresh opaque credential for its synthetic subject and restores configuration after each case. Successful mutations also check the stored receipt and confirmed lifecycle state.

[Committed report, source identities and reproduction](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/blob/3045719435ee12f89018151d735c14b9de2000b8/docs/AUTHENTICATED_V1_RECEIPTS.md) links the exact workflow and baseline/candidate output artifact. The unchanged manifest resolved Express 4.22.3, cors 2.8.6, dotenv 16.6.1, morgan 1.12.1 and uuid 9.0.1; this branch has no dependency lockfile.

## Validation boundary

The earlier credential implementation's execution remains tied to `fcb73610`; the results above establish its composition with the receipt correction at `e5ac9060`. The original credential, policy, provider, accounting, lifecycle, schema and fixture files are unchanged by that composition.

Validation covers the local mock service. Live wallets, Stellar transactions, frontend browser sessions and production deployment were not exercised. The linked passing job is the source-pinned validation carrier; it does not establish the state of the sponsor repository's separate workflow or maintainer acceptance.
